articles.title: How Cristiano Jr. could represent other countries in international football as Ronaldo’s dispute with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus rumbles on
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo’s escalating dispute with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus has put the veteran forward’s international future under the spotlight, but a
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo’s escalating dispute with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus has put the veteran forward’s international future under the spotlight, but a different question surrounds the next generation of the Ronaldo family. His 16-year-old son, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr., has already represented Portugal at youth level, yet the teenager could potentially have been chosen from three other countries because of his family background and birthplace.While Ronaldo Sr. and Jesus remain embroiled in a reported disagreement over the forward’s playing time, Cristiano Jr. has continued his development with Portugal’s youth sides. The teenager has represented the European nation at Under-15 and Under-16 levels, scoring five goals in 13 appearances, according to Portuguese Football Federation records.His decision to play for Portugal at junior level comes despite potential international pathways through Spain and the United States, while reports have also highlighted his Cape Verdean ancestry. The choice is particularly intriguing given that his father’s relationship with Portugal’s senior setup has become a talking point.For now, however, Cristiano Jr. has committed himself to Portugal’s youth pathway. His appearances at that level do not necessarily mean that his international future is permanently settled under FIFA’s eligibility regulations.Ronaldo's row with Portugal coach puts spotlight on familyRonaldo Sr. and Jesus reportedly fell out after the Portugal coach left the veteran forward on the substitutes’ bench during a UEFA Nations League match against Norway. The incident was followed by Ronaldo’s departure from the national team camp and a strongly worded statement in which he accused the coach of repeatedly breaking promises concerning his playing time.The disagreement has raised questions about how the relationship between the two can be repaired before the next international break in November. Whether the dispute has any bearing on Ronaldo’s longer-term involvement with Portugal remains uncertain.The situation has also created an unusual backdrop for discussions about his son’s international future. While the senior Ronaldo has spent much of his career representing Portugal, Cristiano Jr. is still at an age when his footballing development and international prospects could evolve.There is no indication that the teenager’s decision to represent Portugal at youth level has anything to do with his father’s current disagreement with Jesus. Nevertheless, the contrast is striking: the father is dealing with tension inside the senior setup, while the son is building his own international career with the same country.How Cristiano Jr. could have options beyond PortugalCristiano Jr. currently plays in the academy system of Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr, having previously developed at Juventus and Manchester United during different stages of his father’s career. A right-footed left winger, he has been progressing through Portugal’s youth ranks.But his birthplace and family connections have opened up other potential international routes.United States: Cristiano Jr. was born in California, giving him a potential connection to the United States. His birthplace is one of the key reasons the teenager has been discussed as someone who could have had an international future outside Portugal.Spain: The youngster spent more than five years in Spain while his father played for Real Madrid. That period of residence has also brought Spain into the discussion surrounding his eligibility, although residence alone does not automatically establish the right to represent a country under FIFA rules. The applicable eligibility requirements must be met.Cape Verde: Spanish newspaper AS has reported that Cristiano Jr. has Cape Verdean ancestry through his father's grandmother. However, ancestry alone does not guarantee eligibility to represent a country under FIFA regulations. Reports have suggested that he does not meet the applicable conditions for representing Cape Verde, although that eligibility assessment would need to be independently verified.The identity and nationality of Cristiano Jr.'s mother have not been publicly confirmed, leaving open questions about whether he could have an additional international eligibility route through her. However, without verified information about her nationality and the relevant eligibility requirements, it would be speculative to identify another country he could represent.Has Cristiano Jr. already committed his international future to Portugal?Cristiano Jr. made his international debut in a 3-2 victory over Croatia at the Vlatko Markovic tournament in May last year. He has since featured for Portugal's Under-15 and Under-16 sides, making a promising start to his youth international career.His five goals in 13 appearances underline his early contribution, although his development remains a work in progress. At 16, he has time to improve his game, progress through the age-group levels and potentially work towards senior international football.Representing a country at youth level does not always amount to an irrevocable commitment to its senior side. FIFA's eligibility and change-of-association regulations determine whether a player can switch, depending on factors such as the matches played, the nature of those appearances, the player's age and the relevant nationality requirements.That means Cristiano Jr.'s appearances for Portugal should not automatically be interpreted as proof that he can never represent another country. Equally, the existence of possible alternative connections does not mean a switch would necessarily be permitted or that he intends to pursue one.For now, Portugal remains the country he has represented internationally, and there is no confirmed indication that he is considering a change.Ronaldo's Portugal legacy — and his dream for his sonThe contrast between father and son is considerable. Ronaldo Sr. has scored 146 goals in 234 appearances for Portugal, establishing himself as the country's record goalscorer and one of the most influential players in its history.He captained Portugal to their first major international title at Euro 2016 and subsequently celebrated further success in the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025. His relationship with the national side has spanned generations of players and multiple managerial eras.Cristiano Jr., by comparison, is only beginning his journey. He has followed his father through the academies of several major clubs and is now developing at Al-Nassr, where the challenge will be to build a footballing identity of his own.Ronaldo has previously spoken openly about wanting his son to become a professional footballer, while insisting that the decision should ultimately belong to the teenager.In an interview with DAZN in 2018, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner described his son as competitive and said he saw similarities between them.“He doesn't like to lose and he will be like me, I'm sure, 100 per cent,” Ronaldo said. “I like to teach him some stuff, but he's going to be whatever he wants and I'm always going to support him.”Ronaldo also made clear that he hoped his son would follow him into professional football, pointing to the youngster's speed, skills and shooting ability.“But, as you know, he's going to take his decision and he's so young. I'm not going to put pressure on him, but of course I dream to see my boy a football player,” he added.For Cristiano Jr., the immediate task is to continue progressing on the pitch rather than make decisions about senior international football. Portugal has already been his choice at youth level, but his future will depend on his development, his own preferences and the eligibility rules that govern any potential change.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: FSU's Mike Norvell Takes Blame for 'Extremely Poor Performance' in Loss to Louisville
articles.summary: Florida State coach Mike Norvell said the buck stops with him following a 44-20 loss to Louisville on Friday night.
articles.body:
Florida State coach Mike Norvell said the buck stops with him following a 44-20 loss to Louisville on Friday night.

"An extremely poor performance by us," Norvell told reporters after the game. "We started the game well. We jumped up 14-0, but too many missed opportunities. ... Too many times, we didn't show the detail, the discipline, the mental toughness that's necessary on the road. And it starts with me."

The Seminoles jumped ahead 14-0 in the first quarter following a pair of touchdowns from quarterback Ashton Daniels. They proceeded to allow 35 unanswered points.

Louisville running back Isaac Brown had 235 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries. His 97-yard scamper in the second quarter, which came after a goal-line stand, sparked the Cardinals' comeback.

"What we put out there, obviously, guys were not as prepared as they need to be," Norvell said. "But we all need to take ownership of it. Coaches, players, everyone involved. There was plenty of opportunity."

Brown had been quiet through Louisville's first four games but then went off for 125 yards against North Carolina State a week ago. The junior is presumably somebody Norvell and his staff spotlighted.

On the other side of the ball, Daniels' output (21-of-37 for 209 yards, two touchdowns and an interception) was a little underwhelming against a Cardinals defense that's allowing more than 250 passing yards per game.

For Norvell, this might be the point of no return.

Florida State is 3-3 with No. 4 Miami on tap on Oct. 17. Matchups against Clemson, No. 25 Pittsburgh and No. 16 Florida remain as well.

The Seminoles aren't going to make the College Football Playoff — not that anyone expected them to. An 8-4 or 7-5 finish isn't going to cut it, either, when Norvell has just a .532 winning percentage at the helm.

Norvell's buyout is so substantial that it could take some time for the athletic department to get the funds together, even if it's ready right now to make a change.

But it increasingly feels like he's on borrowed time.

articles.title: The substitutes keep delivering
articles.summary: Against Werder Bremen on Friday, Maximilian Beier and Marcel Sabitzer were the only two BVB field players in head coach Niko Kovac’s starting lineup who hadn...
articles.body:
Against Werder Bremen on Friday, Maximilian Beier and Marcel Sabitzer were the only two BVB field players in head coach Niko Kovac's starting lineup who hadn't recently been away on international duty. For Sabitzer, it was actually his first start of the 2026–27 season.

The duo replaced Julian Ryerson as a winger and Konstantinos Karetsas in the attacking midfield role. Both players had returned from international duty carrying injuries; Ryerson wasn't even named to the matchday roster.

In an otherwise lackluster first half, it was Beier and Sabitzer who made the biggest impact for the Black and Yellows with their shots just before halftime. Their shots in the 41st and 43rd minutes were both stopped by visiting goalkeeper Karl Hein; Sabitzer had previously sent a free kick from 27 meters just wide of the Werder goal.

Even after the break, the Austrian remained one of Borussia's driving forces and key players; after 71 minutes on the field, he had 51 touches, covered 8.2 kilometers, and taken four shots on goal – the most of any player on the field at that point, by the way.

"I was very satisfied with his performance. He had two or three good chances. He's an important part of the team," said Niko Kovac, praising the 32-year-old after the match.

Sabitzer was replaced in the closing stages by Konstantinos Karetsas, who had returned to Dortmund quite worn out after four recent appearances with the Greek national team.

Just moments after the 18-year-old entered the game, the four-goal spectacle in the closing stages began. Karetsas played a part in BVB's first goal. Before the 1-0, the young Greek player perfectly initiated BVB's counterattack in their own stadium with a long diagonal pass to Serhou Guirassy. Guirassy then laid the ball back to Fábio Silva, who had also come on as a substitute. Silva's shot turned out to be a perfect assist for the onrushing Daniel Svensson, who gave BVB the lead with his first goal of the season.

Particularly noteworthy: BVB's second goal was also set up by a substitute – namely, Joey Veerman. The Dutchman, who had come on at the same time as Karetsas, took the corner kick in the 85th minute, which Nico Schlotterbeck headed home to make it 2-0.

BVB Substitutes Have Already Toothed Eight Scoring Points

For Dortmund's substitutes, the two assists from Fábio Silva and Joey Veerman – which led to the 2-0 lead – already marked their seventh and eighth direct goal contributions in the current Bundesliga season.

BVB players who came off the bench have contributed three goals and five assists. An excellent tally that impressively underscores what head coach Niko Kovac highlighted after the match as the key takeaway from the game against Werder Bremen : "We're going to need all our players in the coming weeks. Everyone needs minutes under their belt to keep performance levels high and ensure success."

With no fewer than nine competitive matches in 29 days, this broad distribution of success will continue to be crucial for mastering the challenges in the Bundesliga, the UEFA Champions League, and the DFB-Pokal. Next up for BVB in the Champions League is Norwegian champion FK Bodø/Glimt (Oct. 14, 9 p.m., live on DAZN ), followed by away matches against 1. FC Union Berlin in the Bundesliga (Oct. 17, 3:30 p.m., live on Sky ) and Sabah FC in the Champions League (Oct. 20, 6:45 p.m., live on DAZN ). Mats-Yannick Roth

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo wants to score his final 1,000th goal in Portugal shirt: How a six-month ban could ruin his ultimate career dream
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo faces a potential six-month ban following his walkout from the Portugal national team, jeopardizing his dream of scoring his 1,000th career goal in a Portugal shirt. Discover how this suspension could affect Ronaldo’s career aspirations and Portugal’s international matches.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has apologised for walking out on Portugal, accepted that his actions should carry consequences and insisted he remains ready to represent his country. However, the fallout from his dispute with Jorge Jesus has now reached a new stage, with the Portuguese captain provisionally suspended and facing a potential ban ranging from one to six months. Meanwhile, the 41-year-old continues scoring for Al-Nassr, moving closer to the 1,000-goal milestone he has been chasing throughout the latter stages of his career.Ronaldo provisionally suspended after Portugal walkoutAccording to ESPN and the Mirror, Portuguese Football Federation disciplinary regulations have triggered an automatic provisional suspension following Ronaldo's departure from the national team camp, although the final duration of the punishment has yet to be determined.The FPF's Disciplinary Council must still meet to decide the specific penalty, with reports suggesting that Ronaldo could receive a suspension ranging from one to six months. The assessment is expected to consider the circumstances surrounding his departure, his limited involvement during the international window and the public apology he subsequently issued.The dispute began after Ronaldo played in Portugal's 1-0 Nations League victory over Wales before remaining an unused substitute in the following 2-1 win against Norway, despite warming up for approximately 30 minutes.Jesus later explained that he had considered bringing Ronaldo onto the pitch but ultimately decided against it, prompting a disagreement that continued after the match. An emergency meeting involving Ronaldo, Jesus and Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença failed to prevent the forward from leaving the camp ahead of Portugal's 4-2 victory over Denmark.Portugal have since secured qualification for the 2026–27 UEFA Nations League quarter-finals after winning all four of their Group A4 matches, leaving Ronaldo's disciplinary situation as one of the outstanding issues surrounding the national team.Ronaldo apologised and accepted that punishment could followRonaldo addressed the dispute in a lengthy statement published on his social media channels on October 6, explaining his version of the conversations with Jesus and detailing why he eventually decided to leave the camp.The Al-Nassr forward claimed that Jesus had promised to acknowledge publicly that leaving him out against Norway after asking him to warm up had been a mistake. Ronaldo said the coach failed to honour that agreement during the subsequent press conference, prompting him to lose trust in the situation.Although Ronaldo defended his reasons for leaving, he also accepted responsibility for walking away from his teammates and failing to greet the supporters after the Norway match.“I also apologise to my national team teammates for leaving the training camp. For despite my complete breach of the coach's trust, as everyone who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done that. The responsibility rests on me alone,” Ronaldo wrote.He also acknowledged that the federation had grounds to consider disciplinary action, despite his belief that Jesus had broken his promise.“The Portuguese Football Federation must assess the consequences of my actions and punish me for them. I believe the penalty should not be reduced. I am not just an ordinary player; I am the captain of the team, and that is an aggravating factor.”Ronaldo added that he understood the need for consequences and would remain available for Portugal after serving whatever suspension the federation ultimately imposes.“Therefore, if I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team. This is, believe me, the purest of truths.” Ronaldo concluded.What a one-month, three-month or six-month ban would meanThe length of Ronaldo's suspension will determine whether he misses Portugal's next international fixtures against Wales and Denmark, scheduled for November 14 and 17 respectively.According to the reports, a suspension lasting one month would allow Ronaldo to return in time for those matches, provided the ban begins and expires within the expected period. A longer punishment would rule him out of the November fixtures, forcing Jesus to continue without his captain during the next stage of the Nations League group campaign.A three-month suspension, for example, would sideline Ronaldo for those two matches but could still leave him available for the quarter-finals in March 2027, assuming the punishment expires as expected before that stage begins.A six-month ban would carry considerably greater consequences, potentially keeping Ronaldo out until April 2027 and making him unavailable for Portugal's March quarter-final fixtures. Such a punishment would extend the fallout beyond the immediate dispute and could disrupt his involvement in a crucial part of Portugal's Nations League campaign.However, ESPN has suggested that a shorter suspension is more likely, with the disciplinary council expected to weigh Ronaldo's public apology and his long record of service to Portugal when determining the final penalty.The federation has not yet confirmed the length of the ban, meaning Ronaldo's availability for the November matches remains dependent on the decision.Also read: Cristiano Ronaldo has only one personal ambition that could make him swallow his pride and return to PortugalRonaldo reaches 980 career goals despite the uncertaintyWhile his international future remains unresolved, Ronaldo has continued doing what he does best at club level, adding another goal to his extraordinary career tally during Al-Nassr's Saudi Pro League meeting with Al-Diriyah on Friday, October 9.Ronaldo scored in the 23rd minute of Al-Nassr's 3-0 victory, reacting quickest after Kingsley Coman's attacking move produced a save from the goalkeeper before firing the rebound into the net.The goal took Ronaldo to 980 official career goals, leaving him just 20 short of the 1,000-goal milestone he has been pursuing. Samú Costa and Coman also scored as Al-Nassr secured an important league victory.Ronaldo has scored a record 146 goals in 234 appearances for Portugal, and he remains intent on representing his country once he has served any punishment imposed by the federation. That determination may be particularly important given his ambition to reach another historic milestone in international colours.With 980 career goals to his name, Ronaldo is just 20 away from the coveted 1,000-goal mark. Portuguese journalist Miguel Pereira has previously reported that the forward wants to achieve the feat in a Portugal shirt rather than for Al-Nassr, adding another layer of significance to his continued involvement with the national team. Any suspension could therefore complicate his pursuit of a milestone he hopes to celebrate not just as a personal achievement, but in his country's colours.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: German luge greats Wendl/Arlt to continue until 2030 Olympics
articles.summary: Record Olympic luge champions Tobias Wendl and Tobias Arlt of Germany have put their retirement plans on hold and want to continue until the next Games 2030...
articles.body:
Record Olympic luge champions Tobias Wendl and Tobias Arlt of Germany have put their retirement plans on hold and want to continue until the next Games 2030 in the French Alps.

Wendl and Arlt had originally planned to end their careers after the upcominmg 2026-27 season but have changed their mind.

"We are 39, we are fit and healthy," Wendl told broadcasters ZDF.

The two said in an Instagram video: "We have achieved everything in our sport: we are seven-time Olympic champions, 10-time world champions and we have won the World Cup seven times. Our career ends at almost 40 - supposedly. We are starting the project 2030 Olympics and we are taking you along for the ride."

Wendl and Arlt won double luge and team event gold at the 2014, 2018 and 2022 Games, plus team gold and double luge bronze this year at Milan/Cortina.

articles.body: El atacante internacional inglés Cole Palmer ha firmado un nuevo contrato con el Chelsea hasta 2034, con lo que cumplirá once años en Stamford Bridge, informó el club londinense este sábado en un comunicado. Palmer, de 24 años y que llegó al cuadro 'blue' en 2023 procedente del Manchester City -con el que ganó la Liga de Campeones-, ha marcado desde entonces 91 tantos en 138 partidos, en los que, entre otros logros, consiguió el Mundial de Clubes y la Liga Conferencia, ambos en 2025. "El Chelsea significa mucho para mí y creo que el club va por el buen camino, así que estoy encantado de renovar y, obviamente, muy feliz. Tras hablar con los propietarios, con los directores deportivos y, obviamente, con el entrenador, me transmitieron mucha confianza, así que lo más lógico era firmar", afirmó el internacional inglés. "Hablando con los jugadores, todos comparten las mismas ambiciones. Siento que ganamos títulos importantes aquí con regularidad y quiero formar parte de eso y desempeñar un papel fundamental", añadió Palmer, que en estos inicios de temporada ha logrado cuatro tantos y ha dado dos pases de gol.

articles.title: Javier Aguirre: “La gente está expectante a ver si este mexicano le da la vuelta al Valencia"
articles.standfirst: El veterano técnico debuta en El Sardinero con urgencias
articles.summary: El veterano técnico debuta en El Sardinero con urgencias
articles.body: El debut de Javier Aguirre como entrenador del Valencia se acerca. El mexicano se estrena este domingo en El Sardinero ante el Racing de Santander con muchas urgencias en la mochila. El club de Mestalla solo ha sumado 4 de los 21 puntos posibles, siendo penúltimo en la tabla, por lo que la necesidad de sumar es imperiosa. Aguirre compareció en rueda de prensa previa al encuentro y dejó muy claro que en su equipo no negociará el esfuerzo. Su Valencia tendrá el sello que le ha acompañado durante toda su trayectoria. En su comparecencia pública, el mexicano habló del sistema, de las bajas, de los problemas con el peso de Harvey Elliot y de la irrupción de los canteranos que han aparecido en las últimas jornadas en el primer equipo. ¿Qué le dicen cuando le paran por la calle?: "No tengo redes sociales, estuve caminando. El que me reconoce me saluda con mucho cariño. Es impublicable lo que me dicen... la gente está como expectante a ver si es verdad que este mexicano es capaz de darle la vuelta al Valencia... He notado, que no sois hostiles pudiendo serlo, estoy tranquilo, no me tengo que esconder por la calle... la gente está con muchas ganas, muy contenta." Órdenes de Aguirre: "Te diría que no soy de escribir mis conversaciones, lo que me nace, lo suelto, y a veces son burradas. No hay una consigna especial, no llego a tanto, digo lo que siento en el momento. Del día 24 a día de hoy he hablado mucho individualmente y a nivel grupal para que entiendan la idea futbolística y la necesidad que tenemos de puntos. El fútbol es una mesa de cuatro patas y a veces nos olvidamos del factor mental, los jugadores son seres humanos, y yo soy muy parlachín en mi día a día." Problemas con el peso de Elliot: "Tengo la fortuna de que me comunico en su idioma. Le veo más fino, está trabajando con un nutricionista particular. Estoy encantado con su actitud, tiene mucha calidad y es un jugador del Valencia CF. Hay que sacar el mejor provecho posible de él." Danjuma sí, Rioja no: "Los sistemas son dinámicos; pasan dos minutos y haces otra foto y es otra formación. Son números telefónicos. Sí, intentamos meter a un jugador entre centrales… estamos probando cosas para ver qué es lo que mejor le va al equipo. Rioja no llega seguro, hace muchas cosas, pero creo que no lo voy a llevar. A Danjuma sí." Prioridad en el inicio: "El equipo tiene ganas de mostrarse, tiene ganas de sacar eso desde dentro. No es justo lo que nos ha pasado: derrotas por la mínima y empates con sabor a victoria… Tienen ganas de decirse a sí mismos que son mejores que lo que el marcador demuestra. Físicamente estamos evaluándolo y futbolísticamente no tengo ninguna duda porque tienen muchísima calidad". Sato: "Vi los siete partidos del Valencia y él tuvo participación. Me llamaron de Japón, que aún tengo contactos allí, y él vino, sin jet lag... Me ha gustado mucho su actitud. Es muy técnico. Hablé con él porque está aprendiendo español e inglés rápidamente; el japonés es terriblemente difícil, lo sé por experiencia. Ojalá le encuentre un sitio donde pueda rendir mejor". Principal mandamiento de Aguirre: "Es difícil que en noventa minutos se note algo, pero mis equipos se caracterizan por correr y trabajar mucho; no bajamos la guardia, siempre damos la cara, y nos dejamos hasta la última gota de sudor… llegando al vestidor sin guardarse nada. Nunca verás un equipo mío apático e indolente, y esta no será la excepción." Papel de los jóvenes: "Yo no me fijo en el pasaporte o en la edad, te fijas en la calidad y los tres que han debutado la tienen. Cada semana se van ganando los lugares. No me fijo en si tiene un partido o 200, si lo hizo bien durante la semana, juega. Si algo tiene este equipo, es una buena cantera. Guerra, Jesús... veo el mural de los canteranos internacionales y alucinas de lo que hay ahí." Cómo está el equipo: "Anímicamente está bien, quieren estar ya en el campo. Las fechas FIFA te dan una tregua, pero se hacen largas. Las sensaciones son buenas, en lo anímico y también en lo físico. El equipo será de garantías, bastante fiable."

articles.standfirst: El técnico de la Real ve preparado a su equipo para tener mañana un buen regreso a la competición ante el Dépor, al que no ve como un recién ascendido por sus fichajes
articles.summary: El técnico de la Real ve preparado a su equipo para tener mañana un buen regreso a la competición ante el Dépor, al que no ve como un recién ascendido por sus fichajes
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo no da importancia a que su Real Sociedad pueda volver a la sexta posición 29 meses después, si vence este domingo al Deportivo de A Coruña y el Alavés no supera al Atlético de Madrid, ya que considera que ahora es más relevante ganar puntos, juego y confianza, y que la posición importante es la que ocupas al final de LaLiga. El de Nueva Jersey piensa más en sumar de tres en tres desde este mismo domingo. Matarazzo ve a su plantilla lista para volver a competir, tras el largo parón internacional. “Es mucho tiempo sin fútbol desde el último partido, aunque tuvimos el test del encuentro contra el Athletic. Los futbolistas que han estado con las selecciones han venido bien y mi sensación hoy es que todo el mundo está preparado para regresar a la competición”. Le hemos pedido que valorase la lesión de Aramburu y la recuperación de Héctor Fort de sus molestias. “Héctor ha entrenado hoy por primera vez completo y es una opción en la convocatoria, veremos si para jugar un largo periodo de tiempo . Zubeldia está muy bien, está preparado para jugar. Aramburu tuvo un problema en un sóleo y va a tener que estar parado un tiempo, esperemos que esté de vuelta pronto porque es un jugador importante. ¿Su sustituto? Tenemos algunas opciones, ya lo veréis mañana”. Si gana la Real al Dépor y el Alavés no supera al Atlético, los txuriurdin se colocarían en un sexto puesto que hace dos años y medio no tocan. “Me han dicho sí que podemos volver a puestos europeos después de un tiempo, pero no estamos centrados ahora en eso. Lo importante es donde estamos en la clasificación a final de temporada, no donde estamos ahora. Ahora lo que queremos es ganar puntos, mejorar nuestro rendimiento, aumentar nuestra confianza”. Le hemos dicho que el Dépor no es un recién ascendido al uso, ya que se ha reforzado mucho y sólo ha perdido una jornada de las siete y no a domicilio. “Sí, no es el típico equipo que acaba de subir de la Segunda división. Ha hecho buenos fichajes de calidad en verano, es un buen equipo, ganó al Villarreal y empató contra el Betis, sólo ha perdido un partido y 1-0 con el Sevilla… También tiene un buen entrenador, que tiene claro como jugar al fútbol, tiene 10 puntos como nosotros. ¿Sin Aubameyang? El equipo cambiará algo por las lesiones que ha tenido, pero esperamos un Dépor similar al de las últimas semanas”.
